stops.name: Musée d’Orsay
stops.description: The single big commitment of the day — and it belongs to the morning, before the queues thicken and while the top-floor light is still soft on the paintings. Orsay was a railway station before it was a museum, so the whole collection sits beneath a vaulted glass roof and a giant station clock: Monet and the water-lily years, Degas’ dancers, the Van Gogh room, Renoir’s crowds — the founding hits of Impressionism, all in a couple of unhurried hours. Take it first, and everything the day does afterward — the gardens, the bookshop, the river at dusk — is downhill, on foot, and completely unrushed.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Sant'Eustachio Il Caffè
stops.description: A standing-room coffee bar behind the Pantheon, famous enough to have a queue and quick enough that it never matters. Order at the till first, then hand the receipt across the counter.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Pantheon
stops.description: Still a working building after nineteen centuries, and free to enter. Stand under the oculus rather than around the edges — the whole room is built to send your eye up through that hole in the roof.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: San Luigi dei Francesi
stops.description: The French national church, and three Caravaggios in a side chapel that most visitors walk straight past. Bring coins for the light box, or wait for someone else to feed it.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Campo de' Fiori market
stops.description: A morning market square that turns into a drinking square after dark. Come while the stalls are still up — produce, cheese and *porchetta* — and eat standing.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Piazza Navona
stops.description: Baroque theatre on the footprint of a Roman stadium, which is why it is long and rounded at one end. The cafés on the square charge for the view; the streets one block off do not.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Giolitti
stops.description: A long-running gelateria near the Pantheon with a marble-counter routine: pay first, then order. Ask for panna and they will add it without charging.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Armando al Pantheon
stops.description: A small family-run Roman kitchen beside the Pantheon, doing the four classic pastas without reinventing them. Book: the room is tiny and turns over slowly.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Giardino degli Aranci
stops.description: A walled orange grove on the Aventine with a terrace over the river and the dome. The keyhole in the priory gate next door frames St Peter's exactly; there is usually a short queue for it.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Campidoglio terrace
stops.description: The balcony behind the Capitoline palaces, looking over the Forum with no ticket and no queue. Best at dusk, when the ruins light up and the day crowd has gone.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Trattoria Monti
stops.description: A family kitchen in Monti cooking from the Marche rather than Rome — the tortello with egg yolk is what it is known for. Book ahead; it is small and busy.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Sant’Ignazio
stops.description: A Jesuit church whose dome is painted flat on the ceiling — stand on the marker in the nave and it lifts. Free, small, and over in fifteen minutes.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Jewish Ghetto & Portico d’Ottavia
stops.description: One of the oldest Jewish quarters in Europe, layered straight onto Roman ruins at the Portico d'Ottavia. Bakeries and *carciofi alla giudia*; read the brass stones underfoot.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Capitoline Museums
stops.description: The oldest public museum collection in the world, on the hill Michelangelo laid out. The bronze she-wolf and the colossal marble hand are here, and the terrace looks straight down the Forum.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Roman Forum & Palatine
stops.description: Not a building but a whole flattened city centre, and it reads as rubble until you pick a route through it. The Palatine above is quieter and gives you the Forum from overhead.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: St Peter's Basilica
stops.description: Researched experience; not documented by a firsthand visit.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Castel Sant'Angelo & bridge
stops.description: Hadrian's tomb, later a fortress and papal bolt-hole, with a spiral ramp climbing through the middle of it. The bridge in front is the best-dressed in the city.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

days.title: A day at Ostia Antica
days.purpose: A full day at Ostia Antica — the ancient port, whole and quiet.

stops.name: Ostia Antica
stops.description: Rome's harbour town, abandoned rather than destroyed, so streets, baths and apartment blocks still stand. A half-hour train from Porta San Paolo and a whole day once you are there.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Spanish Steps
stops.description: A staircase that works as a grandstand — sitting on the steps is no longer allowed, so treat it as a passage rather than a rest. The view back down Via Condotti is the point.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Ara Pacis Museum
stops.description: Augustus's altar of peace, sealed inside a modern glass box that is itself part of the argument. Small and quick, and the carved processional frieze repays standing close.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence

stops.name: Piazza del Popolo & Santa Maria
stops.description: The old northern gate of the city, with twin churches framing the road in and two Caravaggios in Santa Maria del Popolo. The Pincio steps go up from the corner.
stops.evidence: Web-researched experience · no firsthand archive evidence
